III.}}|{{sc|of the apostles.}}|297}}</noinclude>temple. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=3}} He, vvhen he had {{ls}}een Peter and Iohn about to enter into the temple, a{{ls}}ked to receiue an almes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=4}} But Peter vvith Iohn looking vpon him, {{ls}}aid, Looke vpon vs. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=5}} But he looked earne{{ls}}tly vpon them, hoping that he {{ls}}hould receiue {{ls}}ome thing of them. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=6}} But Peter {{ls}}aid, Siluer and gold I haue not, but {{sup|‖}} that vvhich I haue, the {{ls}}ame I giue to thee: In the name of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} of Nazareth ari{{ls}}e, and vvalke. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=7}} And taking his right hand, he lifted him vp, and forthvvith his feete and {{ls}}oles vvere made {{ls}}trong. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=8}} And {{ls}}pringing he {{ls}}toode, and vvalked: and vvent in vvith them into the temple vvalking, and leaping, and prai{{ls}}ing God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}} And al the people {{ls}}avv him vvalking and prai{{ls}}ing God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}} And they knevv him, that, it vvas he vvhich {{ls}}ate for almes at the Specious gate of the temple: and they vvere excedingly a{{ls}}tonied and aga{{ls}}t at that that had chaūced to him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}} And as he held Peter and Iohn, al the people ranne to them vnto the porche vvhich is called Salomons, vvondering.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epi{{ls}}tle vpō wene{{ls}}day in Ea{{ls}}ter weeke.}}But Peter {{ls}}eing them, made an{{ls}}vver to the people, Ye men of I{{ls}}raël, vvhy maruel you at this, or vvhy looke you vpon vs, as though {{sup|‖}} by our povver or holines vve haue made this man to vvalke? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}} The God of Abraham, and the God of I{{ls}}aac, and the God of Iacob, the God of our fathers hath glorified his {{ls}}onne {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvhom you in deede deliuered and denied before the face of Pilate, he iudging him to be relea{{ls}}ed. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}} But you denied the holy and the iu{{ls}}t one, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 23, 18.''}}* and a{{ls}}ked a man killer to be giuen vnto you. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}} but the authour of life you killed, vvhom God hath rai{{ls}}ed from the dead, of vvhich vve are vvitne{{ls}}{{ls}}es. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}} And in the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This faith was not the faith of the lame man (for he looked onely for almes) nor a {{ls}}pecial faith of the Apo{{ls}}tles owne {{ls}}aluatiō: but the whole beleefe of Chri{{ls}}tian Religion.}}∷ faith of his name, this man vvhom you {{ls}}ee and knovv, his name hath {{ls}}trengthened: & the faith vvhich is by him, hath giuen this perfect health in the {{ls}}ight of al you.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}} And novv (brethren) I knovv that you did it through ignorance, as al{{ls}}o your princes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}} But God vvho fore{{ls}}hevved by the mouth of al the prophets, that his {{sc|Christ}} {{ls}}hould {{ls}}uffer, hath {{ls}}o fulfilled it. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=19}} Be Penitent therfore & conuert, that your {{ls}}innes may be put out.⊣ {{verse|chapter=3|verse=20}} that, vvhen the times {{ls}}hal come of refre{{ls}}hing by the {{ls}}ight of our Lord, and he {{ls}}hal {{ls}}end him that hath been preached vnto you {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=21}} c {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''c {{lang|grc|ὃν δεῖ οὐρανὸν μὲν δέξασθαι}}''}}∷ vvhom {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Some Heretikes fouly corrupt this place, thus, ''Who mu{{ls}}t be conteined in heauen'', of purpo{{ls}}e (as they prote{{ls}}t) to hold Chri{{ls}}t in heauē, from the B. Sacramēt. ''Beza''. As though his pre{{ls}}ēce there, drew him out of heauen.
